title: Your first program and the dotnet toolchain
body: C# is a statically typed language: the compiler checks every name, type and call before the program runs. The .NET SDK provides the compiler, the runtime and the `dotnet` command. A compile-time error means no program was produced; a runtime exception happens later, while a successfully compiled program executes.

Since .NET 10 you can run a single file directly: save `hello.cs` and run `dotnet run hello.cs`. Larger programs use a project: `dotnet new console -o Hello` creates `Hello.csproj` plus `Program.cs`, and `dotnet run` builds and runs it. `dotnet build` compiles without running, which is the quickest way to check your code. A file-based app can later become a project with `dotnet project convert hello.cs`.

The example uses top-level statements: the statements at the top of one file become the body of the program's entry point. The compiler generates the `Main` method for you. Only one file in a program may contain top-level statements. Older code shows the explicit `static void Main(string[] args)` form inside a class; both compile to the same kind of entry point.

`Console.WriteLine` writes text followed by a newline; `Console.Write` omits the newline. Statements end with a semicolon, and braces group statements into blocks. Identifiers are case-sensitive: `console` and `Console` are different names. `//` starts a comment that runs to the end of the line.

Check that you can explain three outcomes: the compiler rejected the code, the program threw an exception while running, or it ran and printed something unexpected. Each needs a different fix, and reading the exact diagnostic code (for example CS0103, a name that does not exist) is the first step.
challenge: Write a program that prints your name on one line and then the result of 12 * 12 on the next line.
question: What does `dotnet build` do that `dotnet run` also does, but without the final step?
correct: Compiles the project and reports diagnostics without executing it
wrong: Executes the program without compiling it
reasoning: run = build + execute. Use build when you only need the compiler's verdict.
